proposed.text: A coastal barangay in Quezon province uses a simplified metric: waste generation per capita is 0.4 kg/day (local study). A 1,500-person barangay segregates waste at 60% biodegradable, 25% non-recyclable, 10% recyclable, 5% hazardous. Annual total solid waste is 219 metric tons. The barangay plans composting for biodegradable waste at an efficiency rate (wet-to-finished compost ratio) of 3:1. How many metric tons of finished compost can the barangay produce annually?
proposed.rationale: Annual biodegradable mass = 219 MT x 0.60 = 131.4 MT. A wet-to-finished ratio of 3:1 means 3 units of wet biodegradable input yield 1 unit of finished compost, so finished = 131.4 / 3 = 43.8 MT. Correct answer is b. The previously marked answer a (32.85 MT) results from dividing 131.4 by 4 (a 4:1 ratio), which contradicts the explicitly stated 3:1 ratio in the stem. Option c (65.7 MT) results from multiplying by 0.5 (a 2:1 ratio). Option d (98.55 MT) would be the result of dividing 219 MT total by 3 without segregating to the biodegradable fraction. Cross-check: 1,500 persons x 0.4 kg/day x 365 days = 219,000 kg = 219 MT, matching the stated annual total, so the fraction allocation is internally consistent.
proposed.explanation: Composting yield = (annual biodegradable mass) / (wet-to-finished ratio). With 60% biodegradable of 219 MT = 131.4 MT and 3:1 ratio, yield = 131.4 / 3 = 43.8 MT/year.
